original_idea.body:
# Easy-to-Hard Generalization of Critique Skills

**Problem:** Whether critique ability elicited on EASY problems transfers to HARD problems within the same model is untested for open models.

**Direction:** Using FindTheFlaws, few-shot prompt a small open model to critique flawed solutions on easy items, then measure flaw-detection F1 on hard items -- comparing few-shot-on-easy vs few-shot-on-hard vs zero-shot.

**Why it matters:** Easy-to-hard transfer is a candidate route to scalable oversight when humans can only label easy cases.

**Relevant context:** arXiv:2503.22989; arXiv:2407.00215.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: easy-to-hard critique transfer is a candidate route to scalable oversight when humans label only easy cases.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Few-shot critique on an existing annotated benchmark; accessible inference work.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Tightly scoped few-shot-easy vs few-shot-hard vs zero-shot F1 comparison.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Easy-to-hard oversight on public benchmark; external-friendly, weak lab incentive.

novelty.reasoning: Easy-to-hard and CriticGPT exist; the easy-shot critique transfer on open models may be open.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Easy-to-hard studied; critique transfer plausibly open.
